summary: Ecuador's Foreign Ministry lists the countries whose nationals require a visa to enter Ecuador, among them India, the Philippines, Vietnam, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Nigeria, Pakistan, Venezuela and China. Ecuador's Regulation to the Organic Law on Human Mobility says a foreigner who enters Ecuador as a tourist may stay for a maximum of 90 days in a one-year period, and that foreigners from the countries for which Ecuador has established a tourist-visa requirement must apply for the visa at a consular office; the Foreign Ministry's procedure page names those countries as the countries to which Ecuador requires a visa before entry. The UK, Canadian, Australian, French, German, Italian and Polish governments say their citizens can visit without a visa.

overstay.text: Foreigners who entered as tourists with 90 days and exceeded that time without requesting an extension, those who requested an extension and exceeded 180 days, and those who entered with 180 days and exceeded that time are fined one unified basic remuneration. The UK government says overstayers are fined when they leave and are not allowed to return to Ecuador unless they pay the fine before leaving.

idp.text: Ecuador is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). Ecuador's General Regulation to the Organic Law on Land Transport, Traffic and Road Safety (Executive Decree 1196, Official Register Supplement 731 of 2012, Article 137) says foreigners entering with a tourist visa or any non-immigrant visa may drive on licences issued in their countries of origin for the whole stay their migratory status allows, but never for more than six months from entry, and foreigners who need no visa may drive on their home licence during the stay granted on entry, provided the licence is valid. After these periods they may not drive unless they exchange their foreign licence for an Ecuadorian one.

tips.text: The Galápagos Governing Council lists a USD 20 Transit Control Card fee and says it must be paid for each trip; Canada's travel advice says the card is purchased at the Galápagos Governing Council counter in the Quito or Guayaquil airports.

The UK Foreign Office tells British nationals they can visit without a visa for up to 90 days in any 12-month period, that an extension of an extra 90 days must be applied for before the first 90-day period ends or they could be fined, and that overstayers are fined when they leave and cannot return to Ecuador unless they pay before leaving.
Health insurance is mandatory for foreign tourists visiting the Galápagos, according to the UK government; no official source we found states a requirement for the mainland.

Australia's Smartraveller says many parts of Ecuador are at high altitude, that you can develop altitude sickness above 2,500 m, and that your travel insurance should cover emergency evacuation from altitude.

The UK government says the Ecuadorean government has declared a 60-day state of emergency as of 15 September, for security reasons, in eight provinces, and that it will mean greater police and military presence on the streets.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Ecuador?
faq.answer: Ecuador's Foreign Ministry lists the countries whose nationals require a visa to enter Ecuador, among them India, the Philippines, Vietnam, Kenya, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iraq, Libya, Myanmar, Nigeria, North Korea, Pakistan, Senegal, Somalia, Sri Lanka, Syria, Venezuela, Yemen and China. Ecuador's Regulation to the Organic Law on Human Mobility says a foreigner who enters Ecuador as a tourist may stay for a maximum of 90 days in a one-year period, and that foreigners from the countries for which Ecuador has established a tourist-visa requirement must apply for the visa at a consular office; the Foreign Ministry's procedure page names those countries as the countries to which Ecuador requires a visa before entry. The UK, Canadian, Australian, French, German, Italian and Polish governments say their citizens can visit without a visa.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Ecuador?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office tells British nationals they can visit Ecuador without a visa for up to 90 days in any 12-month period, and can pay to extend their stay by an extra 90 days, applying before the first 90-day period ends.

faq.question: What do I need to visit the Galápagos?
faq.answer: The UK government tells British travellers that to enter Galápagos they must have evidence of a hotel booking or an invitation letter from their host, evidence of a return flight to the Ecuadorean mainland, a transit control card bought at their departure airport before checking in, and travel health insurance, which it says is mandatory for foreign tourists. The Galápagos Governing Council says tourists may stay up to 60 days in the year, not extendable, counted from their first entry, and must pay the USD 20 Transit Control Card fee on every trip.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Ecuador?
faq.answer: The UK government tells British travellers that to enter Galápagos they must have travel health insurance, which it says is mandatory for foreign tourists. No official source we found states an insurance requirement for mainland Ecuador.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens still enter Ecuador visa-free?
faq.answer: No. Ecuador's Foreign Ministry lists China among the countries whose nationals require a visa to enter Ecuador. It says the visa application is made only online, through the Ministry's official e-VISAS platform.

faq.question: What currency is used in Ecuador?
faq.answer: The UK government says US dollars and the 5, 10, 25 and 50 centavo coins minted in Ecuador are the only legal currencies.
